issue: FDA product status of peptides (503A Category 1/2; 2026 reversal; PCAC July 2026)
why_it_matters: Whether a peptide may lawfully be compounded on prescription changed twice since 2023: Sept 2023 Category 2 placements, Feb-Apr 2026 removal of ~14 of 19 peptides from Category 2, and a July 23-24, 2026 PCAC vote recommending BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, semax and epitalon over FDA staff objections. Melanotan II, GHRP-2, GHRP-6, LL-37 and PEG-MGF remain Category 2. Nothing is FDA-approved; final rulemaking is pending and a policy reversal is possible.
professional_review: FDA regulatory counsel; pharmacy-law counsel; PharmD medical director
pre_launch_action: Adopt a written formulary policy keyed to FDA 503A category status with change control; exclude Category 2 substances and compounded GLP-1s; document clinical-need rationale per patient for any 503A product.
ongoing_control: Monthly review of FDA 503A bulks page, PCAC dockets and warning-letter feed; formulary change log signed by CMO and counsel.

issue: Drug claims / intended use (unapproved new drug and misbranding)
why_it_matters: Any statement that a peptide or supplement heals, treats, prevents or cures creates a drug intended use under the FDCA; for unapproved peptides there is no human RCT evidence to substantiate efficacy claims, so claims are unlawful under both FDCA and FTC Act.
professional_review: FDA/FTC advertising counsel; scientific claims reviewer
pre_launch_action: Build a claims library with per-claim substantiation files; approved language for 'not FDA-approved' and 'emerging research' framing; ban list of disease/efficacy words.
ongoing_control: Pre-publication compliance review of all content and ads; quarterly claims audit.

issue: 'Research use only' (RUO) positioning
why_it_matters: FDA issued seven warning letters dated Mar 31, 2026 (published Apr 7, 2026) holding that RUO / 'not for human consumption' disclaimers do not negate intended use when marketing describes human effects; Lilly is suing RUO retatrutide sellers; card networks and Stripe treat RUO peptides as prohibited.
pre_launch_action: Prohibit RUO SKUs, drop-shipping and affiliate links to RUO vendors; screen partners and influencers for RUO ties.
ongoing_control: Quarterly partner/affiliate audit; takedown SOP for user-generated RUO content.

issue: Compounded GLP-1s after shortage resolution
why_it_matters: Semaglutide (Feb 2025) and tirzepatide (Dec 2024) shortages resolved; FDA issued 55+ warning letters (Sept 16, 2025), ~30 to telehealth companies (Mar 2026) and ~25 more (Jun 2026); Apr 30, 2026 proposal to exclude semaglutide/tirzepatide/liraglutide from the 503B bulks list; >1,700 adverse events logged; Novo has filed 130+ suits and sued Hims & Hers (Feb 2026).
professional_review: FDA regulatory counsel; pharmacy-law counsel; IP counsel
pre_launch_action: Exclude compounded GLP-1s from formulary; route GLP-1 demand to branded DTC channels (LillyDirect $299-449, NovoCare $199-349, TrumpRx ~$350) via prescribing or affiliate education.
ongoing_control: Monitor FDA 503B rulemaking and brand-owner litigation; annual formulary review.

issue: FTC endorsements and influencer disclosures (16 CFR Part 255, 2023)
why_it_matters: Material connections (payment, free product, employment, ownership) must be clearly and conspicuously disclosed in the same medium; the advertiser is liable for endorsers' unsubstantiated claims and must monitor.
pre_launch_action: Influencer contract template with disclosure and claims clauses; disclosure SOP (#ad in-frame, verbal disclosure in video); pre-approval of scripts.
ongoing_control: Monthly monitoring log of influencer posts; remediation and termination procedure.

issue: Celebrity / owner endorsements
why_it_matters: A celebrity co-founder or investor is materially connected; every endorsement, including founder-story content, must disclose ownership; brand bears liability for the celebrity's claims; right-of-publicity and morality clauses govern usage and termination.
pre_launch_action: Endorsement agreement with FTC disclosure clause, claims-approval rights, category exclusivity, morality and reverse-morality clauses, NIL grant with AI-replica carve-outs, indemnities.
ongoing_control: Compliance training for talent; quarterly review of talent content.

issue: Testimonials and consumer reviews (16 CFR Part 465)
why_it_matters: FTC's Consumer Reviews and Testimonials Rule (effective Oct 21, 2024) makes fake, AI-generated, insider or suppressed reviews civil-penalty violations; NextMed (2025) was charged with fake reviews and testimonials from non-customers.
pre_launch_action: Review-collection SOP (no incentives conditioned on positive reviews, no suppression); verify testimonial authorship; disclose generally expected results.
ongoing_control: Quarterly review-platform audit; complaint log.

issue: Before/after imagery
why_it_matters: Before/after photos are efficacy claims requiring substantiation and typical-results disclosure; Meta and TikTok restrict them in weight-loss ads; NextMed used before/after pictures of non-customers.
pre_launch_action: Default ban on before/after in paid media; if used, only real patients with signed consent, dated images, and typical-results disclosure.
ongoing_control: Creative review checklist; platform policy monitoring.

issue: Auto-renewal / negative option (ROSCA, FTC rulemaking, CA ARL)
why_it_matters: FTC Click-to-Cancel rule vacated Jul 8, 2025 (8th Cir.); FTC ANPRM Mar 11, 2026 (comments closed Apr 13, 2026); ROSCA and state laws (California AB 2863 effective Jul 1, 2025; NY GBL 527-a; others) still require clear disclosure, express consent, easy same-medium cancellation and reminders; FTC and states sued Hims & Hers over subscription billing (2026).
pre_launch_action: Checkout with all-in pricing, affirmative consent checkbox, one-click online cancel, confirmation and renewal reminder emails, documented refund policy.
ongoing_control: Track cancellation friction metrics and complaints; annual state ARL law refresh; monitor FTC rulemaking.

issue: Pricing transparency and hidden fees
why_it_matters: NextMed order (final Dec 3, 2025) prohibits misrepresenting cost of telehealth services; 'from $79/month' ads that omit medication, labs, membership terms and early-termination fees are deceptive.
pre_launch_action: All-in price disclosure standard for every offer; itemize what membership includes and excludes.
ongoing_control: Monthly ad audit against pricing standard.

issue: Corporate practice of medicine (CPOM) and MSO / friendly-PC structure
why_it_matters: CA, NY, TX and NJ prohibit lay control of medical practice; MSO may provide non-clinical services for fair-market-value fees only; 2025-2026 state legislation (e.g., Oregon SB 951) is tightening MSO control features; non-compliance voids contracts and exposes licensees to discipline.
professional_review: Health-regulatory counsel in each launch state
pre_launch_action: Form PC(s) owned by licensed physician(s); MSA with clinical-independence provisions; succession/continuity agreements compliant with each state; state-by-state CPOM opinion.
ongoing_control: Annual structure review; clinical governance committee minutes; monitor state legislation.

issue: Fee-splitting and anti-kickback
why_it_matters: Percentage-of-revenue MSO fees and marketing fees tied to prescriptions violate state fee-splitting statutes (CA B&P 650; NY Educ. Law 6531; TX Occ. Code ch. 102; NJ 13:35-6.16); federal AKS applies if federal payors are involved; EKRA and state all-payor statutes can reach cash-pay referrals.
pre_launch_action: Fixed or FMV-based MSO fees documented by valuation; no compensation tied to prescription volume; affiliate payouts limited to non-Rx products.
ongoing_control: Annual FMV refresh; compensation audit.

issue: State medical practice standards and telehealth modality (sync vs async)
why_it_matters: Prescribers must be licensed in the patient's state and meet that state's standard of care; several states restrict questionnaire-only/asynchronous prescribing or require a synchronous encounter before a first prescription; boards have disciplined async GLP-1 prescribing.
professional_review: Telehealth counsel; state medical board rules review
pre_launch_action: State launch matrix (licensure, modality, consent, prescribing rules); default to synchronous video for initial visits; clinical protocols per state.
ongoing_control: Quarterly matrix refresh; license tracking system; chart audits.

issue: Telehealth informed consent
why_it_matters: Most states require documented informed consent to telehealth (e.g., CA B&P 2290.5; TX Occ. Code 111.002), including limitations of remote care, privacy, and emergency procedures; missing consent is a licensure and UDAP exposure.
pre_launch_action: State-specific consent forms captured in intake with audit trail; identity verification.
ongoing_control: Annual consent-form refresh; audit of consent capture rate.

issue: Provider licensure and credentialing
why_it_matters: Each prescriber must hold an active license in the patient's state (IMLC can speed multistate licensure); credentialing, DEA registration (if any controlled substances), NPI, malpractice verification and OIG exclusion checks are expected by boards, insurers and LegitScript.
pre_launch_action: Credentialing file per clinician; license map matching launch states; geofenced scheduling.
ongoing_control: Monthly license/exclusion monitoring; annual re-credentialing.

issue: Controlled substances (Ryan Haight Act / DEA telemedicine rules)
why_it_matters: DEA/HHS fourth temporary extension (Federal Register Dec 31, 2025) keeps tele-prescribing flexibilities through Dec 31, 2026; special registration not finalized. Peptides and GLP-1s are not controlled, so this applies only if the formulary adds testosterone/anabolic steroids (Schedule III); HGH is separately restricted under 21 U.S.C. 333(e).
pre_launch_action: Formulary policy excluding controlled substances and HGH at launch.
ongoing_control: Monitor DEA rulemaking before any formulary expansion.

issue: Pharmacy licensure (non-resident pharmacy; 503A/503B partner diligence)
why_it_matters: Partner pharmacies must hold non-resident licenses in every ship-to state, comply with USP <797>/<795> and 503A interstate-distribution limits (5% / MOU), and state-specific restrictions (e.g., Louisiana Board of Pharmacy on semaglutide-class compounding); state AGs (38 jurisdictions) are pressing FDA and boards on compounded GLP-1s.
pre_launch_action: Partner due-diligence checklist (licenses per state, inspection history, 483s/warning letters, CoA/potency testing, recall plan); contractual licensure warranties and audit rights.
ongoing_control: Quarterly license verification; annual on-site or virtual audit; complaint/AE feed from partner.

issue: Rx fulfillment, labeling and patient-specific compounding
why_it_matters: 503A compounding requires a valid patient-specific prescription and documented clinical need; 'essentially a copy' of an approved drug (e.g., PT-141/bremelanotide, tesamorelin) is prohibited absent a significant difference; FDA's 2025-2026 warning letters cite claims that compounded products are FDA-approved, 'the same as' brand, or safer.
pre_launch_action: Prescription templates with clinical-need documentation; patient labeling and disclosure that products are compounded and not FDA-approved; no bulk/office-stock dispensing.
ongoing_control: Chart audit sample monthly; labeling review on formulary change.

issue: Cold chain, traceability and product quality
why_it_matters: Peptides and GLP-1s are temperature-sensitive sterile injectables; degradation, potency variance and contamination drive the >1,700 adverse events FDA logged for compounded GLP-1s and the impurity allegations in Novo v. Hims; brands can face negligent-marketing claims.
pre_launch_action: Validated cold-chain shipping with temperature indicators; lot-level traceability; CoA retention; recall SOP.
ongoing_control: Excursion log review; supplier scorecards; annual recall drill.

issue: Adverse-event handling and pharmacovigilance
why_it_matters: Compounded and off-label products lack labeling; MedWatch reporting flows through pharmacies but the brand needs intake, triage and escalation; failure to act on AEs is evidence in product-liability and board actions.
pre_launch_action: AE intake channel (phone/app), triage protocol, MedWatch/partner reporting workflow, patient safety communications template.
ongoing_control: Monthly AE review meeting; trend analysis; formulary action on signals.

issue: HIPAA (clinical data in the telehealth entity and MSO)
why_it_matters: The PC is a covered entity and the MSO/platform a business associate; Privacy and Security Rules, BAAs, and the pending 2025 Security Rule overhaul apply; marketing use of PHI requires authorization; pixel sharing of PHI is an OCR and class-action exposure.
pre_launch_action: BAAs with all vendors; risk analysis; access controls; no marketing pixels on authenticated patient pages; NPP and authorizations.
ongoing_control: Annual risk analysis; workforce training; breach response plan testing.

issue: FTC Health Breach Notification Rule (non-HIPAA health data)
why_it_matters: 2024 amendments (effective Jul 29, 2024) cover health apps and sites collecting health information; unauthorized disclosure (e.g., ad pixels) is a 'breach' requiring notice; GoodRx ($1.5M), BetterHelp ($7.8M) and Cerebral (~$7M) are precedents; FTC/state suit against Hims & Hers (2026) alleges health-data sharing.
pre_launch_action: Data map of quiz/intake/membership health data; consent-gated pixels; no sharing of health data with ad platforms; breach-notification playbook.
ongoing_control: Quarterly pixel/tag audit; vendor data-flow review.

issue: State consumer health data laws (WA MHMDA, NV, CT, NY NYHIPA pending)
why_it_matters: Washington MHMDA (private right of action) and Nevada/Connecticut laws require a separate consumer-health-data policy, opt-in consent for collection/sharing and signed authorization for sale; New York's NYHIPA was vetoed Dec 19, 2025 but reintroduced (S9269/A10357) in 2026 and remains pending.
pre_launch_action: Consumer-health-data privacy policy; opt-in consent flows on quizzes and health preferences; no geofencing; data-sale authorization template.
ongoing_control: Monitor NY and other state bills; annual policy refresh.

issue: CCPA/CPRA and other comprehensive state privacy laws
why_it_matters: Health data is sensitive personal information under CPRA (right to limit use); ad-pixel sharing is a 'sale/share' requiring opt-out and GPC honoring; CPPA regulations on risk assessments, cybersecurity audits and ADMT phase in from 2026; 15+ other states have comprehensive laws with sensitive-data opt-in.
pre_launch_action: Privacy notice with CPRA disclosures; opt-out/GPC mechanism; DSAR workflow; risk assessment for sensitive-data processing.
ongoing_control: Annual privacy audit; cookie consent management review.

issue: TCPA / SMS marketing
why_it_matters: FCC one-to-one consent rule vacated (11th Cir., Jan 24, 2025) and repealed by FCC, but prior express written consent for marketing texts, April 2025 revocation rules, DNC and state mini-TCPAs remain; health-related texts also raise consumer-health-data consent questions.
pre_launch_action: Compliant consent capture with disclosure language and record retention; STOP handling; quiet hours; separate transactional vs marketing streams.
ongoing_control: Monthly consent-record audit; litigation watch on state mini-TCPAs.

issue: CAN-SPAM email marketing
why_it_matters: Commercial email must carry accurate headers/subject lines, physical address and an opt-out honored within 10 business days; health-triggered emails also implicate HBNR and state consumer-health-data consent.
pre_launch_action: ESP configuration with unsubscribe and address; suppression-list process.
ongoing_control: Quarterly deliverability and compliance check.

issue: Payment processing (high-risk merchant category)
why_it_matters: Stripe prohibits pharmaceuticals/pseudo-pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals with harmful claims and unapproved research chemicals, and treats telemedicine as restricted; Mastercard's 2026 BRAM update tightened peptide/nutraceutical enforcement; account closures come with 90-180-day reserves.
pre_launch_action: Select a health-vertical acquirer with disclosed MCC and reserve terms; obtain LegitScript before applying; separate MIDs for supplements, membership and Rx services.
ongoing_control: Chargeback ratio monitoring (<0.9%); network mandate tracking (Visa/Mastercard subscription rules).

issue: Ad-platform restrictions (Meta, Google, TikTok, Amazon, LegitScript)
why_it_matters: Meta's health-and-wellness data-source restrictions (from early 2025, expanding 2026) block purchase-event optimization; Google requires LegitScript/NABP certification for Rx/telehealth ads and permits recurring-billing Rx promotion for certified merchants from Mar 31, 2026; TikTok bars Rx ads; Amazon requires supplement testing and bars peptides.
professional_review: LegitScript certification consultant; platform policy specialist
pre_launch_action: Apply for LegitScript (telehealth/healthcare merchant) and Google/Meta certifications; configure Meta events for restricted account; build measurement on top-of-funnel and modelled conversions.
ongoing_control: Monthly policy-change review; ad-account health monitoring; creative pre-screen.

issue: Accessibility (ADA Title III / WCAG)
why_it_matters: 3,117 federal web-accessibility suits in 2025 (+27%), 36% of all federal Title III filings; DTC health sites are frequent targets; WCAG 2.1 AA is the litigation benchmark and 2.2 AA best practice; DOJ Title II rule (2024) signals the standard.
professional_review: Accessibility auditor; ADA defense counsel for statement
pre_launch_action: Build to WCAG 2.2 AA; automated + manual audit including telehealth video and checkout; accessibility statement and feedback channel.
ongoing_control: Quarterly automated scans; annual manual audit; regression tests in CI.

issue: Terms of service, privacy policy and refund policy
why_it_matters: Enforceable terms (arbitration/class waiver, telehealth disclaimers, membership terms, refund rules) reduce class-action exposure; ROSCA and state ARL laws dictate disclosure of cancellation/refund terms; medical disclaimers must not mislead.
pre_launch_action: Clickwrap acceptance with audit trail; separate clinical consent, membership terms, consumer-health-data policy and refund policy.
ongoing_control: Annual terms refresh; version control with acceptance records.

issue: Trademark, right of publicity and NIL
why_it_matters: Brand names must clear USPTO and avoid confusion with pharma marks (Novo/Lilly are litigious, including cease-and-desist campaigns in 2026); using any person's name/likeness in advertising needs written consent under CA Civ. Code 3344 and NY Civil Rights Law 50-51; digital-replica laws (CA 2024; NY) restrict AI likenesses.
pre_launch_action: Clearance search and filings; likeness releases for all UGC/testimonials; no use of brand drug names in a source-identifying way.
ongoing_control: Trademark watch; release checklist in content workflow.

issue: Professional and product liability; D&O; cyber insurance
why_it_matters: Telehealth prescribers need malpractice coverage that includes telemedicine, all licensed states and off-label/compounded products (often excluded); brands marketing compounded products are named in product suits (GLP-1 MDL has 3,200+ federal cases); regulatory investigations require D&O with defense-cost coverage; pixel and breach claims require cyber with regulatory-fines cover.
professional_review: Insurance broker with healthcare/telehealth specialty; coverage counsel
pre_launch_action: Bind malpractice ($1M/$3M per clinician plus entity), products/completed-ops via pharmacy partners with additional-insured status, D&O, tech E&O/media, cyber ($2-5M); confirm no compounded-drug exclusions.
ongoing_control: Annual coverage review against formulary and state footprint; certificate tracking from partners.

issue: Age restrictions and vulnerable populations
why_it_matters: Telehealth prescribing and weight-loss/body-image advertising must be limited to adults (platforms require 18+ targeting); minors' data triggers COPPA and state teen-privacy laws; eating-disorder and body-shaming content is restricted by Meta/TikTok and criticized by regulators.
pre_launch_action: Age gating (18+) at signup and intake; identity verification for Rx; 18+ ad targeting; no minors in creative.
ongoing_control: Audit of age-verification failures; platform targeting review.

issue: Data security program
why_it_matters: HIPAA Security Rule (and its pending overhaul), state breach laws, CPRA cybersecurity-audit regulations and FTC Safeguards-style expectations require documented controls; breaches trigger HBNR/HIPAA/state notices and class actions.
pre_launch_action: Risk assessment; encryption, MFA, logging; vendor security reviews; incident-response plan with notification matrix.
ongoing_control: Annual penetration test and SOC 2 audit; tabletop exercises.

issue: Brand-owner litigation exposure (Novo/Lilly vs telehealth and marketers)
why_it_matters: Novo has filed 130+ suits in 40 states, sued Hims & Hers (Feb 2026, dismissed after partnership), and both Novo and Lilly send cease-and-desist letters to med spas/telehealth; Lilly sues RUO retatrutide sellers under Lanham Act theories; claims that compounded product is 'the same as' brand or use of brand names as source identifiers are the triggers.
pre_launch_action: Brand-name usage guidelines (nominative fair use only); no comparative equivalence claims; cease-and-desist response protocol.
ongoing_control: Litigation watch; quarterly creative review for brand-name usage.

issue: State AG and UDAP enforcement on wellness/GLP-1 marketing
why_it_matters: 38 state and territory AGs urged FDA to act against illegal GLP-1 sales (2025); Mississippi AG issued consumer warnings; state AGs joined the FTC against Hims & Hers (2026); state UDAP statutes allow AG suits and, in many states, private class actions over deceptive health marketing and subscriptions.
pre_launch_action: UDAP review of launch creative and checkout in top-10 launch states; complaint-handling and refund SOP.
ongoing_control: Monitor AG press releases and multistate actions; quarterly complaint trend review.
